> Original MUI X documentation: [Simple Tree View - Customization](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/simple-tree-view/customization/). The examples of this page are written for R.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(muiTreeView)
library(muiMaterial)
library(htmltools)

# Some functions of muiMaterial, muiCharts and reactRouter, used in several examples of this page
pkg_items <- function() {
  list(
    TreeItem(
      itemId = "muiMaterial",
      label = "muiMaterial",
      TreeItem(itemId = "muiMaterial::Button", label = "Button()"),
      TreeItem(itemId = "muiMaterial::TextField", label = "TextField()"),
      TreeItem(itemId = "muiMaterial::Drawer", label = "Drawer()")
    ),
    TreeItem(
      itemId = "muiCharts",
      label = "muiCharts",
      TreeItem(itemId = "muiCharts::BarChart", label = "BarChart()"),
      TreeItem(itemId = "muiCharts::LineChart", label = "LineChart()")
    ),
    TreeItem(
      itemId = "reactRouter",
      label = "reactRouter",
      TreeItem(itemId = "reactRouter::RouterProvider", label = "RouterProvider()"),
      TreeItem(itemId = "reactRouter::Route", label = "Route()"),
      TreeItem(itemId = "reactRouter::NavLink", label = "NavLink()")
    )
  )
}
```

## Basics

### Custom icons

Use the `slots` argument to replace the default icons: `expandIcon`, `collapseIcon`, and `endIcon` for the items without children. A slot expects a React component, which you write with `JS()`. Here, a small helper creates an SVG icon from a [Material icon](https://mui.com/material-ui/material-icons/) path. [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/simple-tree-view/customization/#custom-icons)

```{r}
svg_icon <- function(path) {
  JS(sprintf(
    "(props) => React.createElement('svg',
      { ...props, viewBox: '0 0 24 24', width: 16, height: 16, fill: 'currentColor' },
      React.createElement('path', { d: '%s' }))",
    path
  ))
}

plus_square <- svg_icon("M19 3H5c-1.11 0-2 .9-2 2v14c0 1.1.89 2 2 2h14c1.1 0 2-.9 2-2V5c0-1.1-.9-2-2-2zm0 16H5V5h14v14zm-8-2h2v-4h4v-2h-4V7h-2v4H7v2h4z")
minus_square <- svg_icon("M7 11h10v2H7zm12-8H5c-1.11 0-2 .9-2 2v14c0 1.1.89 2 2 2h14c1.1 0 2-.9 2-2V5c0-1.1-.9-2-2-2zm0 16H5V5h14v14z")
close_square <- svg_icon("M19 19H5V5h14v14zM3 3v18h18V3H3zm14 12.59L15.59 17 12 13.41 8.41 17 7 15.59 10.59 12 7 8.41 8.41 7 12 10.59 15.59 7 17 8.41 13.41 12 17 15.59z")

SimpleTreeView(
  defaultExpandedItems = list("muiMaterial"),
  slots = list(
    expandIcon = plus_square,
    collapseIcon = minus_square,
    endIcon = close_square
  ),
  pkg_items()
)
```

The `slots` argument of a `TreeItem()` changes the icons of one item only: see [Tree Item customization](tree-item-customization.html).

### Custom toggle animations

The `groupTransition` slot of a `TreeItem()` changes the animation used to show the children. The MUI demo uses the `react-spring` library, which is not bundled in **muiTreeView**. [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/simple-tree-view/customization/#custom-toggle-animations)

### Custom styling

Use the `sx` argument to style the tree. Target the parts of the items with their CSS classes (`.MuiTreeItem-content`, `.MuiTreeItem-label`, `.MuiTreeItem-iconContainer`, `.MuiTreeItem-groupTransition`…) and their state with data attributes (`[data-selected]`, `[data-focused]`, `[data-expanded]`, `[data-disabled]`). Colors such as `"primary.main"` come from the [theme](theming.html). [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/simple-tree-view/customization/#custom-styling)

```{r}
SimpleTreeView(
  defaultExpandedItems = list("muiMaterial"),
  sx = list(
    "& .MuiTreeItem-content" = list(
      borderRadius = 2,
      py = 0.5
    ),
    "& .MuiTreeItem-label" = list(
      fontWeight = 500
    ),
    "& .MuiTreeItem-content[data-selected]" = list(
      bgcolor = "primary.main",
      color = "primary.contrastText"
    ),
    "& .MuiTreeItem-iconContainer" = list(
      bgcolor = "action.hover",
      borderRadius = "50%"
    )
  ),
  pkg_items()
)
```

### Custom Tree Item

Use the `slots` and `slotProps` of `TreeItem()` to customize the parts of an item, or replace them with your own components. See [Tree Item customization](tree-item-customization.html). [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/simple-tree-view/customization/#custom-tree-item)

### Headless API

The headless API (`useTreeItem()`) is a React hook. It can be used from R only in a React component written with `JS()`, as shown in [Rich Tree View - Customization](rich-tree-view-customization.html#custom-tree-item). [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/simple-tree-view/customization/#headless-api)

## Common examples

### Connection border

Draw a line between the items of a group by styling `.MuiTreeItem-groupTransition`. [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/simple-tree-view/customization/#connection-border)

```{r}
SimpleTreeView(
  defaultExpandedItems = list("muiMaterial", "reactRouter"),
  sx = list(
    "& .MuiTreeItem-groupTransition" = list(
      ml = "15px",
      pl = "18px",
      borderLeft = "1px dashed",
      borderColor = "divider"
    )
  ),
  pkg_items()
)
```

### Gmail clone

A mail navigation with an icon and a counter on each item. The item labels are muiMaterial `Stack()`s. [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/simple-tree-view/customization/#gmail-clone)

```{r}
mail_label <- function(icon, text, count = NULL, color = "text.secondary") {
  Stack(
    direction = "row",
    alignItems = "center",
    spacing = 1.5,
    sx = list(py = 0.5),
    Box(component = "span", sx = list(color = color), shiny::icon(icon)),
    Typography(text, variant = "body2", sx = list(flexGrow = 1, fontWeight = "inherit")),
    if (!is.null(count)) Typography(count, variant = "caption", color = "inherit")
  )
}

SimpleTreeView(
  defaultExpandedItems = list("categories"),
  defaultSelectedItems = "all-mail",
  sx = list(
    maxWidth = 360,
    "& .MuiTreeItem-content" = list(borderRadius = "0 16px 16px 0", pr = 2),
    "& .MuiTreeItem-content[data-selected]" = list(
      bgcolor = "primary.light",
      color = "primary.contrastText",
      fontWeight = 600
    )
  ),
  TreeItem(itemId = "all-mail", label = mail_label("envelope", "All Mail")),
  TreeItem(itemId = "trash", label = mail_label("trash", "Trash")),
  TreeItem(
    itemId = "categories",
    label = mail_label("tag", "Categories"),
    TreeItem(itemId = "social", label = mail_label("users", "Social", "90", "#1a73e8")),
    TreeItem(itemId = "updates", label = mail_label("circle-info", "Updates", "2,294", "#e3742f")),
    TreeItem(itemId = "forums", label = mail_label("comments", "Forums", "3,566", "#a250f5")),
    TreeItem(itemId = "promotions", label = mail_label("tag", "Promotions", "733", "#3c8039"))
  ),
  TreeItem(itemId = "history", label = mail_label("clock-rotate-left", "History"))
)
```

### Documentation sidebar

The same idea for the sidebar of a documentation website, reusing `mail_label()`: the counters show the number of functions exported by each package, when it is installed.

```{r}
n_exports <- function(pkg) {
  if (requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) length(getNamespaceExports(pkg))
}

SimpleTreeView(
  defaultExpandedItems = list("reference"),
  defaultSelectedItems = "get-started",
  sx = list(
    maxWidth = 360,
    "& .MuiTreeItem-content" = list(borderRadius = "0 16px 16px 0", pr = 2),
    "& .MuiTreeItem-content[data-selected]" = list(
      bgcolor = "primary.light",
      color = "primary.contrastText",
      fontWeight = 600
    )
  ),
  TreeItem(itemId = "get-started", label = mail_label("rocket", "Get started")),
  TreeItem(
    itemId = "reference",
    label = mail_label("book", "Reference"),
    TreeItem(itemId = "ref-muiMaterial", label = mail_label("cube", "muiMaterial", n_exports("muiMaterial"), "#1976d2")),
    TreeItem(itemId = "ref-muiCharts", label = mail_label("chart-column", "muiCharts", n_exports("muiCharts"), "#2e7d32")),
    TreeItem(itemId = "ref-reactRouter", label = mail_label("route", "reactRouter", n_exports("reactRouter"), "#d32f2f"))
  ),
  TreeItem(itemId = "articles", label = mail_label("file-lines", "Articles")),
  TreeItem(itemId = "news", label = mail_label("clock-rotate-left", "Changelog"))
)
```
